prerequisites: Basic knowledge of manufacturing processes, computer science, and statistics is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Acquire knowledge related to reliability engineering and its application in industrial maintenance and manufacturing processes, as well as the study of the useful life of industrial components, machinery, and systems.
Acquire basic technical knowledge for developing Maintenance Management functions in manufacturing and production systems, especially those related to planning and quality management.
Acquire knowledge about new approaches to total maintenance management.
Understand the use of new metrological technologies for maintenance and production and manufacturing processes.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and their clear and succinct presentation.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and time and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for finding sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability to work collaboratively and capacity for the development of multidisciplinary projects.
Ability to incorporate new knowledge in the area of Industrial Engineering, based on acquired training and necessary for the evolution of technology.

syllabus_topics: Definition, objectives, and tools for Total Productive Maintenance (TPM).
New technologies and advanced maintenance approaches.
teaching_methods: Exposition, explanation, and exemplification of content.
Lectures and exercise solving with student participation and specialized software.
Company and/or facility visits (subject to availability).
Personal study of theoretical and practical content.
Preparation of practical reports, assignments, and/or problem sets proposed by the professor, including those requiring software use.
Active methodologies (virtual sessions and/or synchronous or asynchronous modules for practical work, autonomous and teamwork).
Classroom activities (individual and/or group-based, subject to continuous evaluation).
Tutorials (in-person or virtual) and email/messaging support.

assessment_methods.method: Exams (written, in-person or via Virtual Campus)
Supervised practical work, seminars, and laboratory tests (physical and/or software-based)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum grade on the exams, not exceeding 5 out of 10 points, is required. Students who do not meet this minimum will not pass the course, with a maximum final grade of 4.5 out of 10. For those who meet the minimum, the final grade is a weighted average of all assessment elements. Grades from continuous assessment components (other than exams) are retained for the second attempt if exams are not passed in the first attempt. Optionally, written exams in the ordinary call may be replaced by individual projects with oral presentations for a limited number of students; otherwise, students who do not pass must take a final exam in the extraordinary call. Plagiarism will result in a zero grade for the affected activity.
